summary: Join our training course on GIS and Remote Sensing for climate change impact analysis. Equip yourself with essential skills for effective adaptation strategies.
lede: GIS and remote sensing support climate impact analysis by mapping hazards, environmental change and vulnerability. Designed for professionals in resilience, infrastructure planning and risk management, this course develops practical skills in processing satellite data, calculating vegetation and temperature indicators, and creating flood and multi-hazard risk maps. Learners also combine hazard layers with socio-economic information to inform adaptation planning and spatial decisions.
audienceIntro: This program is designed for professionals responsible for environmental resilience, infrastructure planning, and strategic risk management who must integrate spatial intelligence into climate response.
modules: Climate Science Foundations and Geospatial Data
Remote Sensing for Environmental Stress Detection
Spatial Decision Support for Adaptation Planning
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of GIS concepts (layers, projections, and vector/raster data) and basic experience with software such as QGIS or ArcGIS Pro®. No prior experience in climate modeling or programming is required, though familiarity with environmental science principles is beneficial. Participants must bring a laptop with QGIS (latest stable version) pre-installed.
